title: File upstream pdftract codegen-template fix for Swift method naming (ADR-1)
description:
ADR-1 (docs/plan/plan.md) follow-up, P2, cross-repo.

The root cause of the PascalCase-vs-lowerCamelCase method name mismatch (see the compatibility-shim bead) is in the pdftract codegen templates that generate Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift in this repo -- those templates live in jedarden/pdftract, not in pdftract-swift. This bead is a tracking pointer since pdftract-swift's own .beads workspace is where the defect was found; the actual fix needs to happen in jedarden/pdftract's Swift codegen template.

Fix: emit lowerCamelCase method names directly (extract, extractText, extractMarkdown, extractStream, search, getMetadata, hash, classify, verifyReceipt) per Swift API Design Guidelines (methods/functions are lowerCamelCase; only types are UpperCamelCase).

Once that ships and pdftract-swift is regenerated with corrected names, delete the interim compatibility shim (Sources/Pdftract/CompatibilityAPI.swift, added by the other P0 bead in this workspace) in the same PR that picks up the regenerated output.

title: Replace VerifyReceipt's fragile stdout string check with structured JSON parsing
description:
Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift, VerifyReceipt(_:receipt:): runs the CLI's verify-receipt subcommand without --json and checks the result by trimming stdout and comparing to the literal string true.

This is inconsistent with every other method in this SDK, which all pass --json and decode a typed model, and it discards whatever detail the CLI might report about why a receipt failed verification (which of several checks failed, expected vs actual hash, etc) -- the caller only ever learns true or false.

Fix: pass --json to the verify-receipt invocation (assuming the pdftract CLI supports it there, same as extract/hash/classify) and decode a small structured result type (e.g. valid: Bool, reason: String?) instead of doing a raw string comparison on trimmed stdout.

Source: Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift is marked GENERATED -- fix needs to land in the pdftract codegen template (jedarden/pdftract); note the cross-repo dependency when resolving.

title: Surface silently-dropped malformed JSON lines in ExtractStream/Search
description:
Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift, both ExtractStream and Search: when a line from the CLI's NDJSON output fails JSON decoding, the catch block is empty except for a comment (// Skip malformed lines; the final error will be reported if needed / // Skip malformed lines) -- the line is dropped with zero signal to the caller.

Effect: a truncated write, a CLI bug emitting a malformed line, or a schema drift between the CLI and this SDK's Page/Match models all look identical to clean output that simply had fewer pages/matches than expected -- there's no way for a caller to distinguish silently-lost data from a PDF that genuinely had fewer results.

Fix: at minimum, surface a count of skipped/undecodable lines (e.g. via a side-channel callback, a final summary value, or by finishing the stream with a warning-carrying error type) instead of swallowing decode failures unconditionally.

Source: Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift is marked GENERATED -- fix needs to land in the pdftract codegen template (jedarden/pdftract); note the cross-repo dependency when resolving.

title: pdftract-swift origin remote is github.com directly, not Forgejo (hosting policy deviation)
description:
Discovered during 2026-07-20 artifact-improvement audit: this repo's only git remote is origin -> https://github.com/jedarden/pdftract-swift.git. It has no Forgejo (git.ardenone.com) presence detected (a probe to https://git.ardenone.com/api/v1/repos/jedarden/pdftract-swift returned 403, not repo data), which deviates from the workspace-wide policy in CLAUDE.md: all repos hosted on Forgejo as source of truth, GitHub is a read-only mirror synced by Forgejo's server-side push mirror.

This audit committed docs/plan/plan.md (ADR-1 and this bead list) locally but deliberately did NOT push it, to avoid pushing to a github.com remote directly per the ground rule against that.

Resolution needs a human decision: either (a) this repo is intentionally GitHub-native (it's a public SwiftPM package and the README's install URL already points at github.com/jedarden/pdftract-swift, so there may be a deliberate reason it was never migrated), in which case document that exception explicitly somewhere (e.g. a note in this file's CLAUDE.md-equivalent or a per-repo exception list) and the pending local commit can simply be pushed to origin as-is; or (b) it should be brought into the standard pattern by following the 4-step recipe in CLAUDE.md (create Forgejo repo, set local origin to Forgejo, set up a push_mirror from Forgejo to the existing GitHub repo, push there instead) -- note the GitHub repo already has history (not empty), so step 2 of the documented recipe (create GitHub repo empty) doesn't apply verbatim; the existing GitHub history and the Forgejo copy would need to match exactly before enabling the mirror.

Until this is resolved, docs/plan/plan.md's ADR-1 commit (8ea5b02 on main, as of this bead's filing) sits unpushed on the lab checkout at ~/pdftract-swift.

title: Add Argo Workflows CI template for pdftract-swift (swift build + build-tests gate)
description:
ADR-1 (docs/plan/plan.md) follow-up, P0.

pdftract-swift has zero CI today -- no GitHub Actions (disabled workspace-wide per policy) and no Argo Workflows WorkflowTemplate exists for it in jedarden/declarative-config's k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/. This is how a build-breaking defect (see the compatibility-shim bead) shipped to the public repo undetected.

Add a WorkflowTemplate (pdftract-swift-build, following the pattern of forge-ci / needle-ci / spaxel-build already in k8s/iad-ci/argo-workflows/ in declarative-config) that on every push to main:
1. Runs swift build on a Linux Swift image (need to identify/build a Swift-capable builder image -- none of the current templates use one).
2. Runs swift build --build-tests to catch compile breaks in the test target (this specific class of bug -- see the compatibility-shim bead -- would have been caught by this alone).

This repo change goes in jedarden/declarative-config, not in pdftract-swift itself, and must go through the normal ArgoCD GitOps flow (commit to declarative-config, let argo-workflows-ns-iad-ci sync it) -- do not create the Workflow by hand on the cluster.

See ADR-1 in docs/plan/plan.md for full context.

title: Push v1.1.0 git tag for pdftract-swift once CI is green (ADR-1)
description:
ADR-1 (docs/plan/plan.md) follow-up, P1. Depends on: the compatibility-shim bead and the Argo CI bead (both P0) landing first.

No git tags exist on this repo today (git tag -l and git fetch origin --tags both return nothing), but README.md's install instructions tell consumers to depend on it with:
  .package(url: https://github.com/jedarden/pdftract-swift, from: 1.1.0)
SwiftPM's from: requirement resolves against semver git tags, so following the README's own instructions currently fails outright -- there is nothing to resolve.

Once the CI workflow (separate bead) is in place and green on main (i.e. swift build --build-tests passes, which requires the compatibility shim from the other P0 bead), tag the current main as v1.1.0 and push the tag to origin. Per ADR-1's decision, do not tag before CI is verified green -- a tagged release whose test target does not compile is worse than no tag.

title: Clean up temp file leak in Source.bytes(_:) toArgs() (Types.swift)
description:
Sources/PdftractCodegen/Types.swift, Source.bytes(let data) case in toArgs(): writes the PDF bytes to a new temp file under FileManager.default.temporaryDirectory (pdftract-input-UUID.pdf) so the CLI can read it, but nothing ever deletes that file afterward -- not in toArgs(), not in exec() after the process completes.

Effect: every call using Source.bytes(...) leaks one temp file per invocation, and for sensitive documents passed in-memory specifically to avoid touching disk, the PDF content ends up written to a shared temp directory anyway and stays there.

Fix: track the temp file path created in toArgs() and remove it after exec() (or the streaming equivalents) complete, including on the error path. Source: Sources/PdftractCodegen/Types.swift is marked GENERATED -- fix needs to land in the pdftract codegen template (jedarden/pdftract) to survive regeneration; note the cross-repo dependency when resolving.

title: Add lowerCamelCase compatibility shim for Pdftract Swift API (ADR-1)
description:
ADR-1 (docs/plan/plan.md) follow-up, P0.

Every generated public method in Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift is PascalCase (Extract, ExtractText, ExtractMarkdown, ExtractStream, Search, GetMetadata, Hash, Classify, VerifyReceipt). Every consumer -- README.md's usage examples and Tests/PdftractTests/ConformanceTests.swift -- calls the lowerCamelCase form (extract, extractText, extractMarkdown, extractStream, search, getMetadata, hash, classify, verifyReceipt) exclusively. Swift is case-sensitive, so swift build --build-tests fails on main today, and every README code sample is broken for anyone who copy-pastes it.

Do NOT edit Sources/PdftractCodegen/ -- it is marked GENERATED (do not edit manually, use the code generator to refresh) and hand-edits there vanish on the next codegen run.

Add a new, explicitly non-generated file, e.g. Sources/Pdftract/CompatibilityAPI.swift, with an extension on Pdftract (or PdftractClient) exposing the lowerCamelCase names, each forwarding 1:1 to the corresponding generated PascalCase method (extract -> Extract, extractText -> ExtractText, etc). Verify Tests/PdftractTests/ConformanceTests.swift now compiles and the README examples type-check.

This is a prerequisite for filing the upstream generator-template fix (separate bead) and for tagging a release (separate bead) -- see ADR-1 in docs/plan/plan.md.

title: Cache resolved pdftract binary path and verify it is executable
description:
Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift, Pdftract.findBinary(): rescans the full PATH (FileManager.fileExists check only) on every Pdftract() init with no caching, and does not check the found file is actually executable (isExecutableFile(atPath:) would be more correct than fileExists(atPath:)).

Low-severity but easy: cache the resolved path (e.g. a static/lazy var) across instances since PATH doesn't change mid-process for typical server-side use, and switch the existence check to an executability check so a non-executable file with the right name on PATH doesn't get selected and fail confusingly later at exec() time.

Source: Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift is marked GENERATED -- fix needs to land in the pdftract codegen template (jedarden/pdftract); note the cross-repo dependency when resolving.

title: Implement or remove the binary version-compatibility check claimed in README
description:
README.md's Troubleshooting section states: The SDK will refuse to invoke mismatched binary versions. Install the correct version from the releases page.

There is no such check anywhere in the code. .codegen-version (currently 1.1.0) is never read at runtime by Sources/Pdftract or Sources/PdftractCodegen -- grep confirms no reference to codegen-version or any version-comparison logic in exec() or anywhere else. A user running an incompatible pdftract binary gets whatever error the mismatched CLI happens to produce, not a clear refuse-to-invoke message.

Either: (a) implement the check -- e.g. exec() runs pdftract --version once (cached) and compares against the SDK's own .codegen-version, throwing a clear PdftractError before attempting real work on mismatch, or (b) remove the claim from README.md if the check isn't going to be implemented soon, so the docs stop promising a safety net that doesn't exist.

title: Fix Process/Pipe deadlock risk in Methods.swift exec() for large PDF output
description:
Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift's private exec() (used by every non-streaming method: Extract, ExtractText, ExtractMarkdown, GetMetadata, Hash, Classify, VerifyReceipt) calls process.run() then process.waitUntilExit() BEFORE reading from outPipe/errPipe (the reads happen after waitUntilExit() returns).

If the pdftract CLI writes more JSON to stdout than the OS pipe buffer holds (typically 64KB on Linux) -- plausible for a multi-page or image-heavy PDF's --json output -- the child process blocks on write() because nothing is draining the pipe, while the parent is blocked in waitUntilExit() waiting for the child to exit. Classic Process/Pipe deadlock; the call hangs forever (or until a caller-imposed timeout external to this code kills it).

Note this repo's own ExtractStream and Search methods already read the pipe concurrently with the process running (readData(ofLength:) in a while process.isRunning loop) and do not have this bug -- exec() should use the same pattern: drain stdout/stderr concurrently (e.g. via a Task reading while waiting, or Pipe's readabilityHandler) rather than reading only after waitUntilExit().

Source: Sources/PdftractCodegen/Methods.swift is marked GENERATED -- do not edit manually. This needs to be fixed in the pdftract codegen template (jedarden/pdftract) so it propagates on next regen; track that cross-repo dependency in this bead's resolution.
